speaker: Hector
teaser: His left ear runs slow. Odder still, noise seems to help.
hello: Good morning. Hector Ticktock, clockmaker. My left ear has been running slow for years.
And a puzzle for you: I hear better in my noisy workshop than in my quiet parlour.

which_ear.say: The left, no question. It runs about ten years slow. The right still keeps perfect time.
which_ear.note: Left ear worse for years; right ear fine

say: Slowly. Like a clock losing a minute a week.
Ten years, give or take. Nothing sudden. I'd have noticed: I notice everything.
onset.note: Slowly worse over about 10 years, nothing sudden

ringing.say: Yes, in the left. A thin ring, like a chime that never quite finishes. The right is quiet.
ringing.note: Ringing in the LEFT ear only

red_flags.say: No pain, no leaks, no spinning. Unless I stare at a pendulum too long.

noise.say: Eighty clocks ticking, and chimes on the hour. Lively, never loud. No guns, no bands, no power tools.
noise.note: Ticking clocks all day; no loud noise

ear_history.say: Never an infection, never an operation. Never even dropped a screw in there.

say: My mother had an operation on her ear. Back in the seventies.
Afterwards she said the birds had come back. She cried in the garden.
family.note: Mother had an ear operation decades ago

health.say: One little pill for blood pressure. Otherwise sound as a bell. A well-tuned bell.

aids.say: Never. I like to know how a thing ticks before it goes in my ear.

say: At home, in the quiet. My wife sits on my left and murmurs. Gone.
In the workshop everyone shouts over the clocks, and I catch every word! Odd, isn't it?
hardest.note: Trouble: quiet home; fine in noisy workshop

right.caption: Hector's RIGHT ear: a clean canal and a shiny, pearly eardrum.

left.caption: Hector's LEFT ear: just as clean, a normal-looking eardrum. Whatever it is, it's deeper.

tymp.note: Tymp: right type A, left type As (shallow peak)

decision_lines.fit: Not yet! A gap with a stiff, shallow tymp goes to an ear doctor first. Aids can follow.
decision_lines.refer: Refer! A big gap plus a stiff, shallow tymp points to the middle ear. A doctor decides.
decision_lines.today: Nothing sudden: ten slow years, no pain, no dizziness. A doctor soon, not today.
decision_lines.clear: No aids needed? His left ear sits near 60 dB, with a gap. That needs a doctor.

why.prompt: Why does Hector see an ear doctor first?
options: A big air-bone gap and a stiff, shallow tymp on the left.
Yes! A 20 to 35 dB gap plus a stiff tymp points to the middle ear.
Hearing aids can't help a mixed loss.
They can, and often well! But a gap that might be treatable sees a doctor first.
A type As tymp means fluid behind the eardrum.
Fluid reads flat, type B. Shallow but peaked, As, points to a stiff middle ear.
His mother needed an operation, so he does too.
Family history is a clue, not a verdict. The gap and the tymp send him.

debrief: A mixed loss has two parts: bone shows the inner ear's share, the gap shows the middle ear's.
Unmasked bone heard his good right cochlea. Only masked bone showed the left ear's own part.
Gap plus stiff tymp points to the middle ear. Doctor first; aids can come later, or alongside.
goodbye: A letter for the ear doctor, with your chart. The middle-ear part is often treatable.
Same as Mother, then? Her operation gave her the birdsong back.
Maybe, maybe not. The doctor decides that, not an owl.
And my puzzle? Why do I hear better among the clocks?
Over the ticking, people speak up. At home, your wife murmurs on your slow side.
So sit her on your right, and ask people to face you.
Right side, face to face. I'll be back on the dot, Hoot.

headlines.S: CLOCKMAKER'S EAR WOUND TOO TIGHT; OWL REFERS
headlines.A: TICKTOCK'S GAP SPOTTED; DOCTOR ON THE CLOCK
headlines.B: HECTOR REFERRED, BUT A FEW STAMPS RAN SLOW
headlines.C: CLINIC LOSES TIME ON CLOCKMAKER'S CHART
headlines.Do-over: HECTOR RETURNS; CLINIC TURNS BACK THE CLOCK

subheads.S: A mixed loss, masked and measured, with a stiff tymp and a gap: an ear doctor gets the case.
subheads.A: Bone shows the inner-ear part, the gap shows the middle-ear part: refer, and aids can follow.
subheads.B: The gap showed up, but a few steps slipped: mask the bone to prove what is really there.
subheads.C: With a gap on the chart, run the tymp, mask the bone, and send him to a doctor.
subheads.Do-over: Hector will be back, punctual as ever, to the second.
